description:
Execute JavaScript against Xquik's X (Twitter) API at https://xquik.com/docs. search returns endpoints, parameters, and response schemas. The sandbox declares `interface XquikRequest { path: string; method?: "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE"; query?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>; body?: unknown } interface XquikResponse<T> { success: true; status: number; result: T; errors: []; messages: [] } declare const xquik: { result: unknown; request<T = unknown>(options: XquikRequest): Promise<XquikResponse<T>> }`. code is an async arrow function. Canonical result fields use snake_case. camelCase reads resolve to the same value. Missing field reads return undefined and produce warnings listing available keys. Optional fields may require explicit request parameters. An absent field does not prove the data is unavailable. Output holds up to 24,000 characters, so large arrays fit after projection. A longer answer returns its first page. A call may send requests for 54 seconds. Paged reads return a cursor, so a few pages fit 1 call. Independent reads can run together with Promise.all. An answer with a result_id lets a later call project its data through xquik.result. result_id comes only from an earlier answer. It reuses saved data without repeating requests. Authentication and idempotency headers are injected, so code holds no credentials. The sandbox has no filesystem or general network access. A failed request throws an Error naming its method, path, HTTP status and the API's error.

Example
```js
async () => (await xquik.request({ path: "<path from search>" })).result
```

code.description: JavaScript async arrow function that calls xquik.request().

result_id.description: Saved result ID from an earlier answer. Leave it out unless an answer gave you one. Read its data through xquik.result.

name: execute

result.description: JSON returned by the executed async function.

warnings.description: Missing field names mapped to available keys. Optional fields may require explicit request parameters. Absence does not prove the data is unavailable.

title: Execute Xquik API requests
